new_statements.rule_in_words: Default (accent-1) words: stress the penultimate syllable if it is heavy (long vowel or diphthong); otherwise stress the antepenultimate. Words carrying the marked accent 2 (a grammatical final high tone, in Burunge restricted to a few nominal collective suffixes and preverbal clitics) have stress attracted to the high-toned syllable. Stress in Burunge is realised with low pitch in all positions; tone is grammatical, not lexical.
new_statements.exceptions: Accent-2 (high-tone) words override the weight rule — stress goes to the H syllable (typically final). The rule as quoted does not say what happens in disyllables with a light penult (no antepenult); for Proto-West-Rift Kießling says such words stressed the penult (*fála), and the corresponding Burunge treatment is in the unseen grammar pp. 25ff. Endnote 7 flags that Kießling 1994 did not recognise the high-tone collective suffixes that Endl's 2000 data show.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (the paper analyses accent 2 as a word/phrase-level pitch accent whose locus is the terminal syllable of the phonological word). The author's own 2-page summary of the grammar (saved:, p. 1) corroborates: 'Morphological tone overruns the tonal pattern that can be predicted on the basis of the syllable structure and the position of the main stress.'
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Burunge proper (buru1320, ISO bds) as spoken in the Dodoma district; no dialect distinction. Meinhof 1906 calls the language 'Mbulunge' and notes 'Burunge ist nur andere Schreibung statt Mbulunge' (p. 324 fn. 3). The West Rift sisters are Alagwa (alag1248), Gorwaa (goro1270) and Iraqw (iraq1241); Kießling's statement covers Alagwa and Burunge together.
